messages:
Samir: quick update — ran a sticky-prefill separation experiment with a token-lease of 50ms on a small canary (4 hosts) this morning.
Samir: goal was to let the scheduler treat prefill formation independently so kernel selection for decode gets cleaner.
Anika: TL;DR: decode p90 dropped notably, prefill tails got worse. curious about KV behavior. :thinking:
Lee: can you paste the perf snapshot? curious about where the cycles moved.
Samir: posting the short snapshot (copied from perf-collector):
```
stage: prefill_percent=62
stage: decode_percent=28
kernel_crosswalk: mismatch_rate=0.18
kv_hit_rate=0.69
avg_batch_size_prefill=8
avg_batch_size_decode=3
```
Anika: decode p90 85ms -> 60ms, p50 22ms -> 18ms. prefill p95 120ms -> 180ms. overall GPU utilization dropped ~6% but CPU scheduling for prefill spiked.
Maria: that kv_hit_rate 0.69 seems low for our warm mix — did we flush KV priming in the test?
Samir: we intentionally tightened kv-priming window to avoid stale entries during canary — maybe too tight.
Theo: kernel_crosswalk=0.18 suggests we forced a lot of kernel rebinds mid-stream, causing prefill thrash.
Lee: idea: keep token-lease but add a soft-sample for kernel selection that prefers decode-optimized kernels when decode queue depth > X.
Anika: also saw more small prefill batches (avg 8 -> 5 in one run), so the prefill-side batching heuristic collapsed; that increases per-request overhead.
Samir: proposed change set (sketch):
```yaml
# scheduler tweaks
separate_prefill_queue: true
token_lease_ms: 50
kernel_pref_sample: 
  decode_bias_threshold: 12
  sample_fraction: 0.2
kv_priming_window_ms: 200
batch_formation_min_prefill: 6
```
Samir: plan is to run A/B on 6 hosts: A=sticky prefills (current), B=sticky + kernel_pref_sample + larger min_prefill.
Maria: add a metric for "kernel_handoff_rate" and "small_batch_penalty_count" so we can track regressions automatically.
Theo: also instrument queue wait histograms separately for prefill vs decode; right now they get coalesced and we lose signal.
infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: service/inference-scheduler canary v2 on hosts [i-0a...i-0f] starting 2025-03-04T14:20Z.
Lee: one more thought — KV hit-rate sensitivity: if we increase kv_priming_window to improve hits, prefill latency might go down but memory pressure rises; include a kv-eviction counter.
Anika: agreed. I'll run microbench with 1000 synthetic short prompts and 500 long prefills to see how batch shapes evolve.
Samir: action items: Anika run microbench and post results, Lee wire kernel_handoff + small_batch metrics, Maria add kv-eviction + priming gauges, Theo add split queue histograms. We'll reconvene in ~6 hours. :thumbsup:
Lee: noted, I'll add alerts if small_batch_penalty_count > 100 in 5m.
Maria: ping @Samir if you want me to raise a rollback if prefill p95 hits >200ms on prod canary.
Samir: thanks everyone — will post the A/B dashboard link once infra-bot finishes the rollout.
infra-bot: canary rollout 2/6 hosts completed, 0 errors, monitoring for 15m.
Samir: seeing early signals — decode latency improving on host-2 and host-5, prefill spike localized to host-4. investigating host-specific kernel mapping.
Theo: might be NUMA or kernel driver mismatch on host-4, will grab dmesg and kernel logs.
Anika: microbench started, ETA ~45m.
Samir: good. logging this thread for the postmortem notebook.
